formulation.rationale: This split child contains only Toujeo insulin glargine U-300, which current society guidance treats as an ultra-long-acting basal insulin with a longer preprocedure adjustment window than standard U-100 glargine.

passages.locator: Summary of evidence before Important note 11
passages.quote: For patients using ultra-long-acting basal insulins (e.g. glargine U300, degludec), dose adjustments should begin 48 to 72 h before surgery, due to their prolonged pharmacokinetics profiles.

comparisons.checked_locators: Summary of evidence before Important note 11
comparisons.note: The 2026 joint statement explicitly names glargine U-300 as ultra-long-acting and states that dose adjustments should begin 48-72 hours before surgery.

comparisons.checked_locators: Perioperative Care, insulin therapy adjustments; Insulin Therapy Recommendations 16.8 and 16.9
comparisons.note: ADA provides a current class-level long-acting basal-insulin reduction on the evening before surgery and retains basal insulin through NPO and adequate-intake states.

comparisons.checked_locators: Recommendations Before Colonoscopy > Patient Education and Navigation
comparisons.note: USMSTF does not provide a Toujeo-specific dose and directs individualized antihyperglycemic medication planning with the prescribing clinician.

recommendations.timing_text: dose adjustments should begin 48 to 72 h before surgery
recommendations.strength: not separately stated in this evidence statement
recommendations.certainty: not separately stated in this evidence statement
recommendations.applicability: Elective surgery or procedure in a patient receiving insulin glargine U-300.
recommendations.exceptions: The quoted passage specifies the start of adjustment but not the numeric magnitude of U-300 dose reduction; no numeric SBD reduction is inferred.
recommendations.summary: The Brazilian joint statement says glargine U-300 dose adjustments should begin 48-72 hours before surgery.

recommendations.timing_text: On the evening before surgery, reduce long-acting basal insulin analogs to 75–80% of the usual dose
recommendations.strength: not separately graded in this narrative instruction
recommendations.certainty: not separately graded in this narrative instruction
recommendations.applicability: Long-acting basal insulin analogue use before surgery, including glargine U-300 at the class level.
recommendations.exceptions: ADA states that adjustment depends on diabetes type and clinical judgment and does not separately specify U-300 timing.
recommendations.summary: ADA recommends reducing long-acting basal insulin analogues to 75–80% of the usual dose on the evening before surgery.

recommendations.timing_text: Basal insulin or a basal plus bolus correction insulin plan is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Noncritically ill patient with poor oral intake or taking nothing by mouth.
recommendations.exceptions: This supports retention of basal insulin but does not specify a Toujeo U-300 dose.
recommendations.summary: ADA retains basal insulin as part of the preferred insulin plan during poor oral intake or NPO status.

recommendations.qualifier: postprocedure poor oral intake or NPO
recommendations.timing_text: Basal insulin or a basal plus bolus correction insulin plan is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Postprocedure patient with poor oral intake or still NPO.
recommendations.exceptions: No fixed Toujeo restart time is stated.
recommendations.summary: When oral intake remains poor or the patient remains NPO, ADA retains basal insulin in the preferred insulin plan.

recommendations.timing_text: an insulin plan with basal, prandial, and correction components is the preferred treatment
recommendations.applicability: Postprocedure patient with adequate nutritional intake.
recommendations.exceptions: No fixed Toujeo restart time is stated.
recommendations.summary: With adequate nutritional intake, ADA includes basal insulin as part of the preferred insulin plan.

scenario_coverage.reason: SBD/SBA/ABESO provides U-300-specific adjustment timing and ADA provides a class-level basal-insulin dose reduction.
ADA retains basal insulin during NPO or poor oral intake.
ADA includes basal insulin in preferred regimens for poor/NPO and adequate nutritional intake states.

conflicts.description: SBD/SBA/ABESO explicitly says glargine U-300 adjustment should begin 48-72 hours before surgery because of prolonged pharmacokinetics, whereas ADA gives a generic long-acting basal analogue reduction on the evening before surgery. The timing frameworks are preserved separately.

open_questions.text: The SBD/SBA/ABESO U-300 passage specifies when adjustment should begin but not a numeric U-300 reduction; the clinician reviewer must not infer a dose percentage from the standard glargine row.
USMSTF does not provide a colonoscopy-specific Toujeo dose and directs individualized antihyperglycemic management with the prescribing clinician.

editorial.notes: Unreviewed evidence package for insulin glargine U-300 only. The concentration-specific longer adjustment window is preserved; no unsupported numeric SBD U-300 reduction is inferred.
